Elias, I understand you cannot give a clean pass on track 7 as long as the package proposes worldwide digital and physical distribution of all twelve tracks, given that the 'Night Transit' license covers digital-only in the United States and Canada. Tessa, I understand you cannot give a clean pass until the release date is corrected to October 18, 2026, and the credit wording is confirmed to read exactly 'Featuring Inez Vale' across the album listing.

As Music Supervisor, I am the one who makes the binding decision on this album package before artwork and delivery files are finalized. However, given that both of your final checks have identified compliance issues that prevent a clean pass on the current draft, I cannot in good conscience approve the package as proposed.

Here is what I am prepared to decide:

1. The release date must be corrected to October 18, 2026, per the artist agreement Tessa confirmed.
2. The credit wording must read exactly 'Featuring Inez Vale' on the album listing.
3. For track 7, 'Night Transit' — since the license as currently executed only covers digital exploitation in the United States and Canada, I am not willing to approve worldwide digital and physical distribution of all twelve tracks as a single uniform package. Track 7 must either be limited to digital-only in the US and Canada, or the license must be amended to cover the broader scope before I will sign off.

Before I issue a formal settlement, I want to ask both of you directly: Elias, given the options you laid out, is restricting track 7 to digital-only in the US and Canada something that would satisfy your final check, assuming the other tracks proceed under their existing clearances? And Tessa, aside from the release date and credit wording, are there any other compliance concerns on your end that would need to be addressed before you can give a clean pass?

I want to make sure we have everything on the table before I make my binding decision.
